newsitem.title: NORWAY: Orkla profits up on portfolio gains, branded goods.
newsitem.headline: Orkla profits up on portfolio gains, branded goods.

text.p: Norway's food-based conglomerate Orkla ASA said on Thursday that gains in branded goods and its investment portfolio boosted pre-tax profits for the first four months by 35 percent.
The figure, which beat market expectations, rose to 933 million crowns ($130.6 million) from 693 million in the corresponding year-ago period.
The company, which dominates the Nordic branded goods market, said earnings per share increased to 13.50 crowns from 10.10 crowns and that the net profit grew to 648 million crowns from 483 million.
Operating revenue grew to 9.42 billion crowns from 8.31 billion while operating profits increased to 633 million from 514 million.
Orkla booked portfolio gains of 419 million crowns, up from 371 million.

"The financial investments area achieved a return of 16 percent in the first four months, which is 3.2 percentage points higher than the Oslo Stock Exchange All-Share Index," the company said in a statement.
"The branded consumer goods area continues to develop favourably, but profit in the Chemicals area shows a marked decline," it said.
Total branded consumer goods operating profits rose to 405 million crowns from 343 million while chemicals fell to 79 million from 153 million, it said.
Orkla said trends in the most important markets for the branded goods business were mixed in the first four months.
Volumes in the Swedish groceries market remained virtually unchanged while the Norwegian groceries market recorded moderate volume growth.

"Prices are under pressure due to continued competition," it said. "The Group's branded goods businesses have largerly maintained their market positions. However, market shares for beer in Sweden and Norway have decreased slightly."
In the chemicals area, prices of speciality pulp have been on par with prices in the last four months of 1996, but about 21 percent lower than prices in the first four months of 1996, Orkla said.
